proof_nl: Let x be any real number, and set m = floor(x). By the defining property of the floor function, m is an integer such that m <= x < m + 1. Subtracting m from all parts gives 0 <= x - m < 1. By the definition of the fractional part, frac(x) = x - floor(x) = x - m. Therefore 0 <= frac(x) < 1, and also x = floor(x) + frac(x). Since x was arbitrary, the statement holds for every real number x.
